document.abstract: The history of television production and technology has been a continuing process of change and improvement. Changes in technology and the production processes span the time from the early days when programming was either live or film-based, continuing through the changes to videotape, color from monochrome, from analog to digital through to today's solid state storage and high-definition production processes. Throughout most of this change and innovation, the production process was primarily a linear, serial process and the consumer experience largely consisted of a push-based process, involving “appointment” viewing on a single type of viewing device. The current transition to networked, file-based workflows promises to achieve greater flexibility and efficiency to address changes in business and consumer expectations in the media space.

authors.bio: Clyde D. Smith is Senior Vice President of Global Broadcast Technology and Standards for Turner Broadcasting System, Inc. In this capacity, Smith is responsible for the strategic development and planning of new technology, standards and technical practices development, adoption and implementation, to support the Domestic and International News and Entertainment Groups. Previously, as supervisor of Communications Design and Development Engineering for Lockheed Space Operations Company at The Kennedy Space Center, Smith participated in the design team that implemented NASA's improvements of space shuttle transportation systems, following the Challenger accident. Smith held a key role in creating the technology that resulted in Turner Broadcasting System, Inc., being awarded a 2003 Emmy for Outstanding Achievement in Technology and Engineering for “Pioneering Efforts in the Development of Automated, Server-Based Closed Captioning Systems.” In 2006, he received Broadcasting and Cable's Technology Leadership Award. He is a recipient of the SMPTE outstanding service award and the SMPTE Progress Medal recognizing his outstanding technical contributions to the progress of engineering phases of the television industry. At the 2008 Consumer Electronics Show, he received the Storage Visions Conference's “Storage Industry Service Award”. A SMPTE Fellow, Smith has served as Governor, Standards Chair, Secretary/Treasurer, and program chair for four SMPTE Advanced Motion Imaging conferences.
